emma: quick design check — sketch attached in figma but TL;DR: 1) inline threshold editing (click a threshold value to edit in-place) 2) notification preview pane that shows sample payload + delivery channel 3) suppression rules preview (show which alerts would be silenced) liam: love it. main concerns: discoverability of inline edit + mobile layout for the preview pane nadia: can we also show the effective threshold after rounding/aggregation? e.g., 95th p50 vs raw cpu%. users get confused on rollups kevin: agreed on aggregation display. also we need an explicit "preview as" dropdown (service vs team vs global) so sample notifications look accurate emma: yes — thinking a small badge: "previewing: service=audit-worker" that you can change. keeps main canvas uncluttered aria: accessibility nits: inline edits must be keyboard focusable and announce context. Proposed aria flow: ```\n
\n \n
\n``` Also screen reader should read the computed aggregation line: "Computed 95th over 5m: 72%" liam: thanks aria. let's add a small helper tooltip (non-modal) that explains "percentiles are computed on 1m windows then rolled up" — copy task for docs kevin: UX question: do we inline-save on blur or show explicit Save/Cancel? inline-save is faster but risky for mistakes nadia: prefer explicit Save for thresholds. they're critical. but allow quick keyboard shortcut (Enter = save, Esc = cancel) emma: ok Save/Cancel visible when editing. show subtle unsaved indicator on the row (small dot) until saved — helps multi-edit flows liam: preview pane: can we show a small timeline with sample match points and which notification rules would fire? that would help debugging suppression rules kevin: yes a mini-timeline. keep it collapsible. default collapsed on narrow screens aria: color contrast: timeline markers need 4.5:1 for info/warning states. also avoid green/red sole encoding — add shape or icon for colorblind users emma: good call. will add patterned fill + icon overlay. also microcopy tweak: change "Suppress for" to "Silence notifications for" — clearer? liam: shorter is better but "Silence" maybe too aggressive? what about "Mute notifications for" nadia: "Mute" implies temporary. that works for us since suppression is time-bound. good call devops-bot: deployment checklist: add e2e for keyboard flows, screenshot tests for preview pane, and a smoke test that toggles suppression rules kevin: one more: routing preview — show which channel would be used if failover kicks in (e.g., primary email -> fallback slack). show both states in the preview toggler emma: action items: 1) emma to update figma (inline save controls + unsaved dot) 2) aria to write the a11y acceptance criteria 3) kevin to spec mini-timeline and routing preview 4) liam/nadia to draft microcopy options liam: I'll take microcopy and coordinate with docs for a short explainers page. ETA end of week aria: I'll drop the ARIA checklist in this thread by EOD and attach sample NVDA narrations kevin: I'll wireframe the timeline and post annotated screenshots emma: thanks team :thumbsup: will iterate and post updated frames. any other UX edge cases pls shout now nadia: maybe a small "last triggered" timestamp on each rule row so you can quickly see staleness — low effort, high value kevin: +1 emma: noted, adding that to figma liam: excellent. let's demo on Friday design sync. if anyone wants to pair on accessibility testing msg me aria: happy to pair :headphones: kevin: ok closing thread for now, will reopen if new blocking issues crop up
